### Testing Notes / Validation Steps

- [ ] The `deploy` commands should now work.

title: All things add, list, remove.
description:
### Description

This change provides polish to the `add`, `list` and `remove` commands.  It also adds a new `details` command.  See the testing notes below for more details.

More renaming and reordering was done for grouping like things together (sorry for the messy diffs).  The `do_ping()` function is gone now.

The deploy commands now validate the server information if it wasn't retrieved from the store.

The mock Connect server has been updated to produce a more realistic response for the `server_settings` endpoint, including extra data when a valid API key is provided (this means mock endpoints that are marked as authenticated can now also mark that authentication as optional).  The Python versions endpoint was also added.

Connected to https://github.com/rstudio/connect/issues/16430
Connected to https://github.com/rstudio/connect/issues/16423

### Testing Notes / Validation Steps

- [ ] The `rsconnect deploy` command should now work again.
- [ ] The `rsconnect test` command should still produce proper output in all scenarios.

- [ ] For the `add`, `list` and `remove` commands,

    * [ ] The `--help` option should now produce clear and complete help.
    * [ ] Each command should produce sensible output for missing, bad and good arguments in all combinations.

- [ ] The `reconnect details` command should now show clear and complete help with `--help` and should show the correct Connect and Python versions on the requested server (either by nickname or API).
- [ ] Passing an unsaved server to the `deploy` commands will now verify the server and API key similar to the `test` command before attempting to do the deploy.
- [ ] Docstrings have been provided on functions affected by this change.

title: All things test (command, not unit).
description:
### Description

This change provides polish to the `test` command.  See the testing notes below for more
details.

Various function and argument names were renamed for clarity of purpose.  This includes a new
function, `test_server()` that will eventually replace `do_ping()` once the latter is no longer
used.

Connected to https://github.com/rstudio/connect/issues/16428
Connected to https://github.com/rstudio/connect/issues/16423

### Testing Notes / Validation Steps

- [ ] All occurrances of "instance" relating to a Connect server in the CLI help should use the
  word, "server" instead.
- [ ] The `rsconnect add` command should now work again.
- [ ] The `rsconnect test --help` command should now produce clear and complete help.
- [ ] The `rsconnect test` command should now produce proper output in these scenarios:

    * Specifying a server with or without a scheme (i.e., `localhost:3939` should now work
      properly).
    * Specifying a server that is running Connect will show the correct full URL.
    * Specifying a server that is running, but is not Connect, will show an appropriate error.
    * Specifying a bad/non-existent server should show an appropriate error.
    * When a good API key is given, the associated username will be shown.
    * When a bad API key is given, an appropriate error should be shown.

- [ ] Docstrings have been provided on functions affected by this change.

title: Normalize CLI argument usage.
description:
### Description

This change normalizes CLI argument definition and usage.  See the testing notes below for details.

Some general things to note:

- Some command options did not have a short form.  This has been addressed as follows:

    * `--insecure` may now be `-i`
    * `--cacert` may now be `-c`
    * `--python` may now be `-p`
    * `--static` may now be `-S` (capitalized)
    * `--app-id` may now be `-a`

    > **Note:** The short form for the `--new` option to force a new deployment has been changed to `-N` so as not to conflict with the short form of `--name`.

- Help text was standardized to sentences; i.e., periods are now consistently used.

- Function order was rearranged to group related CLI commands together.

Connected to https://github.com/rstudio/connect/issues/16405

### Testing Notes / Validation Steps

- [ ] Running `rsconnect` by itself should now include prose on the CLI's function.
- [ ] Help for `rsconnect test` should be more clear and complete.
- [ ] Help for `rsconnect add` should be more clear and complete.
- [ ] The `rsconnect remove` command now requires that a nickname be specified with `-n`/`--name` and that a server URL be specified with `-s`/`--server` for consistency with other commands.  Specifying neither or both should result in an error.
- [ ] Help for `rsconnect remove` should be more clear and complete.
- [ ] Help for `rsconnect list` should be more clear and complete.
- [ ] The `rsconnect deploy notebook` command now requires that a nickname be specified with `-n`/`--name` and that a server URL be specified with `-s`/`--server` for consistency with other commands.  Specifying neither or both should result in an error.
- [ ] Help for `rsconnect deploy notebook` should be more clear and complete.
- [ ] The `rsconnect deploy manifest` command now requires that a nickname be specified with `-n`/`--name` and that a server URL be specified with `-s`/`--server` for consistency with other commands.  Specifying neither or both should result in an error.
- [ ] Help for `rsconnect deploy manifest` should be more clear and complete.
- [ ] All commands that accept `--insecure` should now accept `-I` also.
- [ ] All commands that accept `--cacert` should now accept `-c` also.
- [ ] All commands that accept `--python` should now accept `-p` also.
- [ ] All commands that accept `--static` should now accept `-S` also.
- [ ] All commands that accept `--app-id` should now accept `-a` also.
- [ ] All commands that accept `--new` should now accept `-N` for force new rather than `-n`, which now means `--name`.

title: Alter user agent to avoid cloudflare's anti-botnet ban
description:
Related: https://github.com/json-schema-org/json-schema-spec/issues/830#issuecomment-571572662

The long and short of this is that cloudflare's "browser integrity check" setting recently updated (pretty much 3 days ago) to block every `Python-urllib` UA. This has already begun to affect folks who are keeping their connect servers behind cloudflare. We also had an unrelated issue with our CI expecting to be able to access json-schema via Python to validate some swagger documents.

Weirdly, this block can be bypassed by merely changing the user-agent header. Therefore:

- New user agent: `rsconnect-python/VERSION` where VERSION comes from `version.txt`.

# Testing Notes

I ran `nc -l 8080` and tried `rsconnect test -s http://localhost:8080` and `rsconnect deploy notebook -s http://localhost:8080 Untitled.ipynb` and checked that netcat reported the correct user-agent header.

title: chore: add support for Python 3.14
description:
## What

Adds Python 3.14 to the supported versions: CI matrix, `just all-tests`, and the changelog. No source changes are needed — `requires-python` is `>=3.8` with no upper bound.

## CI matrix

The ubuntu matrix gains 3.14. The macOS and Windows jobs move from 3.13 to 3.14, so the newest version keeps cross-platform coverage.

## The conftest.py shim

Python 3.14 makes `functools.partial` objects descriptors. httpretty 1.1.4 (the latest release, from 2022) mocks TLS by assigning a partial to the `ssl.SSLContext.wrap_socket` **class attribute**. On 3.14 that partial now binds the context as the first positional argument, and httpretty mistakes it for the socket. This broke every HTTPS test.

`conftest.py` wraps `httpretty.core.fake_wrap_socket` and drops the leading `SSLContext` argument. An `isinstance` check makes it a no-op on 3.13 and earlier.

Tracked for removal in #833, which proposes replacing httpretty with a maintained library (mocket).

## Verification

Full suite run locally on 3.8, 3.13, and 3.14 (macOS):

- **Same tests, same skips.** 768 passed / 12 skipped on both 3.13 and 3.14. The skip *reasons* diff clean, so no new version-gated skips hide behind the totals.
- **Coverage matches.** 83.02% on 3.13 vs 83.01% on 3.14. The single delta is in `rsconnect/pyproject.py`, where five bare field annotations are statements on 3.13 but not on 3.14.

Windows on 3.14 is untested locally, and the shim touches `ssl` and socket mocking — worth watching that job.

Closes nothing; relates to #833.

title: fix: preserve title_is_default in deploy manifest/bundle redeploys
description:
## Summary

`deploy manifest` and `deploy bundle` pre-resolve the content title before constructing `RSConnectExecutor`:

- `rsconnect/main.py` (`deploy_manifest`): `title = title or default_title_from_manifest(file)`
- `rsconnect/main.py` (deploy bundle command): `title = title or default_title_from_bundle(file)`

`RSConnectExecutor.__init__` computes `self.title_is_default = not title`, so these two commands always produced `title_is_default=False`, even when the user never passed `--title`. `RSConnectClient.deploy` then does:

```python
if app["title"] != app_title and not title_is_default:
    result = self.content_update(app_guid, {"title": app_title})  # PATCH v1/content/{guid}
```

Consequences:
- Every redeploy to an existing `--app-id` where the derived default title differs from the server's title issued `PATCH /v1/content/{guid}`.
- Under Connect trusted publishing (machine identities), that endpoint is categorically forbidden, so the whole deploy failed with a 403.
- Under an API key, the content got silently renamed to a junk derived title (e.g. `"inst"` for R manifests with no `metadata.entrypoint`, since `_default_title_from_manifest` falls back to `dirname(manifest_file)` — the cwd basename when deploying `"manifest.json"` by relative path).

Other deploy subcommands (e.g. Python source deploys) were unaffected because they pass `title=None` through to the executor, so `title_is_default=True` and the PATCH is correctly skipped.

## Fix

`RSConnectExecutor.__init__` now accepts an explicit `title_is_default: Optional[bool]` parameter. When provided, it overrides the `not title` inference. `deploy_manifest` and `deploy_bundle` compute `title_is_default = not title` *before* filling in the manifest/bundle-derived default, and pass it through explicitly:

- When the user passes `--title`, behavior is unchanged (title used, `title_is_default=False`).
- When they don't, `title_is_default=True`, so no PATCH is issued on redeploy to an existing `--app-id`.
- New-content creation (no `--app-id`) is unaffected: `RSConnectClient.deploy` forces `title_is_default=False` whenever `app_id is None`, so the manifest/bundle-derived default title is still applied via `content_update` for brand new content, exactly as before.

## Tests

Added to `tests/test_main.py`:
- `test_deploy_manifest_redeploy_preserves_title` — redeploying existing content via `deploy manifest --app-id` without `--title` issues no PATCH, even when the manifest-derived default title differs from the server's title.
- `test_deploy_manifest_redeploy_with_explicit_title_still_updates` — with `--title` explicitly passed, the PATCH still happens when the title differs.
- `test_deploy_bundle_redeploy_preserves_title` — same regression, for `deploy bundle --app-id`.
- `test_deploy_manifest_new_content_uses_manifest_derived_title` — new-content creation (no `--app-id`) still gets its title defaulted from the manifest (`"app5"`, derived from the entrypoint) rather than a generic fallback, and that default is still applied via PATCH after `content_create`.

Verified the first three tests fail on `main` (reproducing the bug) and pass with this fix. Also ran the full `tests/test_main.py` and `tests/test_api.py` suites (134 passed, 12 skipped — the skipped ones require a live Connect server or R), plus `ruff format`/`ruff check` on the touched files.

Added a changelog entry to `docs/CHANGELOG.md` under `## Unreleased`, per this repo's release process (`CONTRIBUTING.md`).

Fixes #835
